outcome: A cast spell's card goes to the stack, while an activated or triggered ability goes on the stack without a card.
Each object put on the stack goes on top of the existing objects, so the last added resolves first.
Objects put on the stack simultaneously go in APNAP order, the active player's lowest, so the non-active player's resolve first.
A spell has its card's characteristics, an ability on the stack has only its text, and each has the controller the rule names.
When all players pass in succession the top stack object resolves, or the step or phase ends if the stack is empty.
Effects do not go on the stack; only delayed triggered abilities they create can, when they trigger.
Static abilities, including characteristic-defining ones, apply continuously without using the stack.
A mana ability resolves immediately without the stack, producing mana and any other effect at once.
Special actions happen immediately without using the stack.
Turn-based actions happen automatically at the start or end of steps without the stack and before priority.
State-based actions happen automatically without the stack before a player would receive priority.
